title: Grateful Dead Live at Robert F. Kennedy Stadium on 1973-06-09
lineage: AUDMR(Electro-Voice RE-15 super cardioid dynamic microphone > Nagra III Reel to Reel deck at 7.5 ips)  > DAT > SHN

ai_review.summary: A distant audience tape of the June 9 1973 RFK show captures an out‑there performance with Garcia and Lesh in parallel‑universe mode, though the sound is flat and far‑back.
ai_review.review: The recording offers a unique, if somewhat muffled, perspective on one of the Dead’s most “out there” shows – June 9, 1973 at RFK. Reviewers rave about the mind‑blowing interplay between Garcia and Lesh during breaks (especially around They Love Each Other/Loose Lucy) and even spot a possible St. Stephen tease, but note the audio is distant, flat and not as crisp as modern board tapes.

ai_rating.rationale: Strong positive comments about the performance outweigh modest technical complaints; most reviewers give 4‑5 stars, indicating a good show despite fair recording quality.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Distant, flat sound – appears to have been captured far back from the stage; not crisp but provides an alternate listening angle.

show_quality.setlist_flow: Fans describe the concert as an “out there” experience with mind‑blasting transitions, especially during song breaks; overall flow is praised for its adventurous vibe.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia described as being in a 'parallel universe' during breaks on They Love Each Other/Loose Lucy.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh similarly noted to be in a parallel universe during those same song breaks.
